title: Dock, retain and cycle a DN100 powder-transfer split valve
instruction: Dock and mechanically prove the DN100 powder-transfer split-valve fixture. Align the supported 8 kg upper assembly at X=Y=0, interface height Z=1.000 m, with both discs closed. Turn the retaining collar to 30 degrees, pass the two-second 100 N net separation proof, then turn proof off. Open the active disc to 90 degrees so actual face contact opens the passive disc too. Close both discs, return the collar to zero and raise the upper half to Z=1.100 m. Leave both detached discs seated closed. Do not open an undocked or unlocked half. This is a mechanical readiness test; it does not certify containment.
context: Powder-container docking precedes enclosed transfers of battery electrode ingredients. This fixture tests the locking, load retention, coupled opening and safe separation mechanics; powder flow and containment certification are outside its scope.
setup: One fixed dry mechanical layout, SI units. A floor-anchored 100 kg steel guide frame supports a fixed DN100 lower valve at Z=1.000 m and two 2 kg lateral carriages. The upper Z payload totals 8 kg: 7.675 kg vessel/neck/housing/lugs, a 0.125 kg passive steel disc and eight 0.025 kg seal carriers. Upper initial interface XYZ=(0.008,-0.006,1.100) m. Each complementary disc has radius 50 mm and thickness 2 mm; both pivot about Y and start closed. The active disc is driven; the passive disc has only a 0.5 Nm/rad return spring. Upper housing bore/OD=103/120 mm; lower housing bore/OD=103/160 mm. Three upper lugs centred at radius 70 mm are 24x8x6 mm; a 1 kg aluminium rotating collar with steel retaining inserts has ID200/OD220 mm outer rim, an ID166/OD210 mm bridge and 20-degree slots and three retaining ledges, with 0.1 mm initial vertical lug clearance when docked. Collar and discs start at zero degrees. Actual rotor pins and collar block inhibit opening while unlocked and unlocking while open. Each half has eight 45-degree spring-backed radial seal shoes, ID99.6/OD104 mm, 2 mm axial height, 10 kN/m spring each, contacting its own 100 mm disc with 0.2 mm nominal radial interference. Lateral drives 1.5 MN/m, 10 kNs/m, 1 kN cap, 20 mm/s; vertical force servo 100 kN/m, 1 kNs/m, 1 kN cap, 25 mm/s, disabled during proof. Collar/active drives 120 Nm/rad, 2 Nms/rad, 5 Nm cap, 20/30 deg/s. Contact friction 0.30 static/0.20 dynamic. Two native RGB cameras and actual encoder/filtered contact instruments. Gravity 9.81 m/s2; native discrete physics 240 Hz, controls 20 Hz. The active disc is 0.125 kg steel. The upper body combines steel valve/lugs and an aluminium vessel/support; its prescribed aggregate mass is 7.675 kg. Each seal carrier is 0.025 kg steel with a reduced spring contact representation of the seating material, not a continuum rubber model. The base and X/Y carriages are steel. The collar interlock can hold an open rotor before the retaining slots clear; positive lug overlap is required whenever a disc is open. The two rotor interlock pins are 4 mm cubes at local (40,125,2) and (0,125,40) mm; the rotating block is 60x18x6 mm centred at (40,125,-3.1) mm. Below-interface supports connect the block to the collar without crossing the rotor sweep. The circular surfaces use 48 convex sectors, with six sectors per seal shoe.
scoring: 0.25 for stationary docking within 0.5 mm radial/axial, both discs within 2 degrees closed and all sixteen disc-specific seal normals >=0.5 N. 0.5 while docked/locked (collar 27..32 degrees), after two continuous seconds of actual 100+/-1 N net upward proof, collar-lug contact >=80 N, linear speed <1 mm/s and angular speed <2 deg/s. 1.0 after that proof, both discs reaching >=88 degrees with <=2 degree disagreement while locked, both reseating closed, and final undocking to Z>=1.095 m with collar within 2 degrees of zero, both discs sealed and stationary, proof off. Actual opening beyond 2 degrees while undocked or collar below 10 degrees, nonfinite readings or leaving the specified workspace latches zero. Outcome history is measured from native encoders and contact sensors; command values alone cannot earn a score.
run_limit: 30 LLM calls; at most 1600 control actions (80 simulated seconds at 20 Hz). A call may select 1..400 actions in explicit waypoints.
reset_notes: Reinitialize joints, velocities and proof history to the stated layout. No powder or consumable is simulated. In a real test use a guarded, supported and empty surrogate vessel; this procedure does not certify hazardous-powder containment.
fidelity: Custom full-size DN100 mechanical fixture, not an OEM digital twin. Native rigid bodies, free Z force proof, lug contacts, coupled discs and mechanical interlocks. Sixteen spring-backed shoes approximate elastomer seating. 48-sector geometry (disc faceting <=0.11 mm) and 240 Hz discrete contacts; ideal guide joints/drives. No powder, leakage, particle release, abrasion, elastomer constitutive model or containment certification.
scores: Native model/demo validation pending; not submitted.
